candidate_analogs.name: Puga Valley & Tso Kar Basin (Ladakh, India)

satellite_provenance.multispectral: ESA Sentinel-2 L2A & NASA ASTER Level 2 Surface Reflectance

candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Hyper-arid high-altitude permafrost valley surrounded by jagged crystalline and metamorphic peaks. Features geothermal sulfur, borax evaporite flats, cryogenic ground polygons, and continuous subsurface permafrost lenses under intense solar UV flux.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Accessible via Leh-Manali Highway (seasonal June-October); military airstrip at Nyoma within 50 km
primary_testing_focus: Subsurface Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) ice lens profiling
Rover traction in cold, rocky permafrost scree slopes
Cryogenic drill bit wear in sulfate-silica-ice cement
Extreme UV sensor calibration and solar panel degradation

candidate_analogs.name: Lonar Impact Crater & Deccan Traps (Maharashtra, India)

satellite_provenance.dem_source: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM & ALOS PALSAR RTC
satellite_provenance.multispectral: NASA ASTER Level 2 Surface Mineralogy & Landsat-9 OLI-2

candidate_analogs.scientific_description: The only hypervelocity impact crater on Earth excavated entirely in Deccan flood basalt. Preserves pristine shock-metamorphosed plagioclase (maskelynite), shatter cones, impact melt spherules, and steep basaltic rim walls mimicking lunar mare impact craters and young Martian calderas.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Paved road access from Aurangabad/Jalna (140 km); year-round field operations
primary_testing_focus: Steep basalt rim descent and autonomous winch rappelling
Wheel abrasion testing on fractured basalt ejecta blocks
In-situ Raman and XRF detection of shocked basalt minerals
Microwave sintering and ISRU testing of flood basalt regolith

candidate_analogs.name: Askja Caldera & Holuhraun Lava Field (Central Highlands, Iceland)
candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Massive, unweathered basalt lava sheet (2014-2015 eruption) mantled by pumice and black volcanic glass sand dunes, directly bordering glacial icecaps. NASA Apollo astronauts (Armstrong, Aldrin) historically trained nearby in the 1960s.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: F-Road 4WD track open July-September; high-clearance expedition vehicles required
primary_testing_focus: Rover suspension traverse over jagged pāhoehoe and 'a'ā clinker basalt
Visual odometry failure rates over homogeneous black basalt sand
Testing sub-ice radar sounders against volcanic ice-layer boundaries
Simulating Artemis VIPER hazard avoidance on steep crater rims

candidate_analogs.name: Lava Beds National Monument & Medicine Lake (California, USA)

coordinates.region: Modoc Plateau / Cascade Volcanic Arc, California

satellite_provenance.thermal: ASTER Thermal Infrared (TIR) Nighttime Cavity Heat Detection

candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Over 800 caves and subterranean conduits carved by Pleistocene fluid basalt flows. Contains vertical collapsed skylight chimneys, intact roofs exceeding 10m thickness, natural radiation-shielded microclimates, and perennial subterranean ice deposits.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Direct highway access, National Park Service research permit infrastructure, developed trailheads
primary_testing_focus: Autonomous 3D LiDAR SLAM mapping without GPS inside pitch-black basalt conduits
Subterranean tethered winch drop testing through 20-30m vertical collapse pits
Mesh-network RF communication repeaters through high-density iron-rich basalt rock
Underground habitat inflatable module pressurization and seal integrity tests

candidate_analogs.name: Danakil Depression & Dallol Hydrothermal (Afar, Ethiopia)

satellite_provenance.multispectral: Sentinel-2 MSI (Iron Oxide/Sulfate indices) & ASTER TIR

candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Lowest subaerial rift on Earth (-125m below sea level). Super-heated brine springs with pH < 0, saturated with iron chloride, elemental sulfur chimneys, potash evaporite deposits, and toxic chlorine/sulfur degassing, mirroring Noachian/Hesperian acid-saline Martian waters.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Remote desert route from Semera/Mekele; armed security escort required by local protocol; extreme thermal environment
primary_testing_focus: Corrosion-resistance testing of rover materials against hyper-acidic sulfuric brines
Deep-UV and Raman biosignature detection in extreme poly-extreme evaporites
Drill mechanism testing through hydrated iron-sulfate salt crusts
Thermal dissipation performance under 50°C+ ambient heat load

candidate_analogs.name: Qaidam Basin Yardangs & Saline Playas (Qinghai, China)
candidate_analogs.classification: Novel Mars Desert, Wind Yardangs & Evaporite Crusts
candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Hyper-arid, high-elevation endorheic basin filled with colossal wind-carved yardang ridges, desiccated smectite clay mudstones, bedded halite-gypsum deposits, and polygonal desiccation cracks closely mimicking Gale and Jezero crater floor morphology.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Accessible from Golmud or Da Qaidam via National Highway G315; vast unpopulated testing ranges
primary_testing_focus: Autonomous rover navigation through maze-like wind yardang corridors
Wheel slippage and sinkage testing in desiccated saline silt deposits
Core drill sampling of stratified clay and sulfate layers
Dust devil tracking and aerodynamic wind erosion modeling

candidate_analogs.name: Alvord Desert & Steens Mountain Basalt (Oregon, USA)
candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Extremely flat, 160 sq km dry alkali playa basin bounded by a 1,500m fault scarp exposing over 60 stacked Miocene flood basalt flows. Features hot springs, borate deposits, and fine-grained silt crusts mimicking flat Martian volcanic plains mantled by dust.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Fields-Denio road access, BLM public lands; ideal for high-speed rover traverse testing
primary_testing_focus: High-speed long-range autonomous rover dead-reckoning and visual SLAM
Radio frequency LOS/NLOS propagation against steep basalt fault cliffs
Solar panel dust clearing wiper testing and electrostatic repulsion
Deployable landing pad anchor pull-out resistance testing

candidate_analogs.name: Salar de Pajonales & Domeyko Basin (Antofagasta, Chile)
candidate_analogs.scientific_description: Hyper-arid high-altitude salar characterized by massive gypsum crusts, inverted stream channels, and subterranean endolithic cyanobacterial micro-niches protected inside translucent halite/gypsum minerals, mirroring late Hesperian Martian lakebeds.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Remote 4WD track from San Pedro de Atacama or Antofagasta; high-altitude acclimatization needed
primary_testing_focus: Subsurface endolithic biosignature identification with fluorescence spectroscopy
Rover coring drill operations inside brittle, interlocking gypsum crusts
Wheel slip modeling in powdery beneath-crust efflorescent salt
Automated sample caching and hermetic seal verification under vacuum-like dryness

candidate_analogs.name: Haughton Impact Crater (Devon Island, Nunavut, Canada)
candidate_analogs.scientific_description: 23-km diameter meteorite impact crater in a polar desert. Features shatter cones, deep impact breccia deposits, continuous permafrost ice-wedges, hydrothermally altered carbonate-sulfate deposits, and extreme Arctic freeze-thaw cycles.

logistics_and_testing.access_viability: Remote charter flight via Resolute Bay; Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station (FMARS) infrastructure
primary_testing_focus: Human spacesuit mobility and ergonomics in extreme cold weather
Rover drivetrain cold-soak and low-temperature battery performance
Permafrost ice-core drilling in shattered limestone-dolomite breccia
Thermal model validation of polar shadowed impact valleys
